deck.name: Vocabulary Builder
deck.description: Useful English words for reading and writing, with clear definitions.

questions.explanation: Merriam-Webster defines ubiquitous as existing everywhere at the same time. Example: Smartphones are ubiquitous in the city.
Merriam-Webster: "lasting a very short time". Example: The rainbow was an ephemeral sight.
Merriam-Webster: "marked by kindness or generosity". Example: A benevolent donor paid the fees.
Merriam-Webster contrasts pragmatic with idealistic. Example: They chose the cheaper repair as a pragmatic solution.
Merriam-Webster: "showing or requiring extreme care and attention to detail". Example: She kept meticulous records.
Merriam-Webster describes using a minimum of words. Example: His laconic reply was a single sentence.
Merriam-Webster: "enjoying the company of others". Example: The gregarious host greeted everyone.
Merriam-Webster includes the sense "to make obscure". Example: Jargon can obfuscate a simple explanation.
Merriam-Webster: "to make better or more tolerable". Example: The changes ameliorated working conditions.
Merriam-Webster links capricious to sudden unpredictable impulses. Example: Capricious weather disrupted the picnic.

choices: Available at a very high price
questions.explanation: Merriam-Webster describes knowledge restricted to a small group. Example: The lecture covered esoteric mathematical ideas.
Merriam-Webster: "showing or suggesting a generous and kind nature". Example: The winner was magnanimous in victory.

questions.answer: A person who flatters someone powerful to gain an advantage.
questions.explanation: Merriam-Webster describes a self-seeking flatterer. Example: The sycophant praised every decision to gain favor.

questions.prompt: "Loquacious" and "garrulous" both describe a very talkative person.
questions.explanation: Merriam-Webster defines both words in terms of talkativeness. Garrulous can suggest excessive or tedious talk.
Merriam-Webster includes "to lessen the vitality or strength of". Example: The exhausting heat enervated the hikers.
Merriam-Webster includes making something less harsh. Example: Shade can mitigate the effects of heat.
Merriam-Webster: "markedly distinct in quality or character". Example: The report combined disparate sources.

choices: Modest in order to blend in
Practical in order to save time
questions.explanation: Merriam-Webster associates ostentatious with conspicuous display. Example: The ostentatious entrance drew every eye.

questions.prompt: She was reticent about her private life. What does reticent mean here?
questions.explanation: Merriam-Webster: "inclined to be silent or uncommunicative in speech". It also records a broader reluctant sense.

choices: Helpful in a lasting and reliable way
Careful in a precise and exacting way
Stubborn in a firm and determined way
Harmful in a subtle or gradual way
questions.explanation: Merriam-Webster describes hidden or easily unnoticed harm. Example: The rumor had a pernicious effect on trust.

choices: Done with little interest or care
Done with unusual skill and care
Done with clear urgency and purpose
Done with strong enthusiasm and pride
questions.explanation: Merriam-Webster: "lacking in interest or enthusiasm". Example: He gave the form a perfunctory glance.

questions.answer: Calmness and composure, especially in a difficult situation.
questions.explanation: Merriam-Webster: "evenness of mind especially under stress". Example: She handled the delay with equanimity.
Merriam-Webster connects quixotic with impractical pursuit of ideals. The word comes from Don Quixote.
Merriam-Webster: "being only partly in existence or operation". Example: The proposal was still inchoate.
Merriam-Webster: "marked by eager hopefulness". Example: She remained sanguine about their chances.
Merriam-Webster: "not needed". Example: The editor removed superfluous words.

choices: Persistent and unwilling to give up
Cautious and unwilling to take risks
Careless and likely to lose interest
questions.explanation: Merriam-Webster connects tenacious with persistence and holding firmly. Example: The tenacious climber kept trying.
Merriam-Webster describes contradictory feelings existing together. Example: She felt ambivalent about leaving home.
Merriam-Webster records candid as honest and sincere in expression. Example: He gave a candid assessment.
Merriam-Webster defines ameliorate as making something better or more tolerable.
Merriam-Webster: "promptness in response". Example: She accepted the invitation with alacrity.
Merriam-Webster describes sustained care and attention. Example: Assiduous practice improved his playing.

choices: Bold and willing to take risks
questions.explanation: Merriam-Webster includes "intrepidly daring". Example: The audacious plan surprised the team.
Merriam-Webster describes harm that may be subtle or unexpected. Example: Pollution had deleterious effects on the stream.
Merriam-Webster: "designed or intended to teach". Example: The didactic tale ends with a moral.
Merriam-Webster links erudite to knowledge gained by study. Example: The erudite historian answered every question.
Merriam-Webster: "extremely or excessively careful or detailed". Example: She was fastidious about punctuation.
Merriam-Webster describes quiet secretive action. Example: He cast a furtive glance at the clock.

questions.prompt: What is an "iconoclast" in its figurative sense?
questions.explanation: Merriam-Webster: "a person who attacks settled beliefs or institutions". Historically the word also concerns destroying religious images.

choices: Too vague to be taken seriously
Too great to express in words
questions.explanation: Merriam-Webster: "incapable of being expressed in words". Example: The view filled her with ineffable joy.

choices: To combine things into a whole
To place things side by side
questions.explanation: Merriam-Webster describes placing different things beside each other, often to compare or contrast them.

questions.prompt: What does "liminal" mean when describing a stage of life?
questions.explanation: Merriam-Webster includes an intermediate state or condition. Example: Graduation can feel like a liminal moment.
Merriam-Webster links mendacious to deception or falsehood. Example: The mendacious account concealed what happened.
Merriam-Webster includes resistance to persuasion. Example: He remained obdurate despite their appeals.

questions.prompt: Her pellucid explanation helped everyone understand. What does "pellucid" mean here?
questions.explanation: Merriam-Webster includes "easy to understand". The word can also describe transparent clarity in a material.

questions.prompt: The solution was prosaic rather than exciting. What does "prosaic" mean here?
questions.explanation: Merriam-Webster includes the senses ordinary and unimaginative. Prosaic can also mean relating to prose.

questions.prompt: The room was redolent of cedar. What does "redolent" mean here?
questions.explanation: Merriam-Webster includes being full of a fragrance. Redolent can also mean strongly evocative of something.
Merriam-Webster includes chance changes and hardships. Example: They faced the vicissitudes of a long career.

questions.prompt: The speech was anodyne and upset no one. What does "anodyne" mean here?
choices: Likely to provoke a strong dispute
Unlikely to offend or cause tension
questions.explanation: Merriam-Webster: "not likely to offend or arouse tensions". Anodyne also has a pain-relieving sense.

questions.prompt: What is an "aberration" from a usual pattern?
choices: A repetition of what is expected
A correction of an earlier mistake
A summary of a common sequence
A departure from what is normal
questions.explanation: Merriam-Webster describes deviation from a normal state. Example: The unusually cold day was an aberration.
